critical_finding: ALL motors fire NOSE-FIRST (forward). The 'retro' motor is NOT producing retrograde thrust. OpenRocket applies motor thrust along the rocket's longitudinal axis regardless of motor mount name or position. The current 3+1 cage configuration cannot produce retro braking.

gate1_causal_language.correction: K550W produced lower touchdown speed in tested runs. Physical cause unresolved until thrust direction proven.

gate3_retro_thrust_vector.finding: All 3 tested motors (K550W at 3.0s, K550W at 5.0s, H180W at 4.0s) INCREASE velocity. Thrust is NOSE-FIRST. Motor mount position/name does not reverse thrust direction.
gate3_retro_thrust_vector.conclusion: OpenRocket applies motor thrust along the rocket longitudinal axis. The motor mount configuration cannot produce retrograde thrust. The current design is fundamentally incapable of powered braking.

implications: The OSIFOG 'retro' motor concept requires physical motor reversal, not just delayed ignition
OpenRocket InnerTube motor mounts always fire nose-first
No motor delay timing can produce braking with the current mount configuration
The 3+1 cage has all 4 motors firing forward — the 'retro' motor adds ascent thrust
To achieve retro braking, the motor mount must be physically reversed (180° rotation)
OpenRocket may support reversed motor mounts via component orientation — needs investigation
blocking_reason: Retro thrust direction is wrong. No powered landing search can succeed until the motor fires in the correct direction.
